| 1 | main talk | Title | Title. Say: this is the Oct 25 update. Main results are on Amazon Reviews 2023 Electronics only. The headline system is now a frozen LLaMA probe plus an Evidence model, combined by a Reflector. |
| 2 | main talk | The Problem: Why Single-Pass LLMs Fail | Problem. Single-pass LLM rating has no evidence check. Keep it short: 1 minute. |
| 3 | main talk | The Paper We Chose: What It Does | The paper we chose. Four cards, left to right: the task (one model rates a review 1-5 and justifies it), the data steps (TextBlob cleaning, equal per star, varied wording, extra neutral), the model (LLaMA-3-8B with a small LoRA add-on, exact Table 1 settings), and the prompt (rubric, one example, step-by-step). Then the reported 92.6%. Say: we rebuilt exactly this as Phase 1. |
| 4 | main talk | Why It Falls Short | Why it falls short. Four reasons in plain words: one pass with nothing to catch mistakes; the score depends heavily on the set-up (a leaked example, a skewed test, leak-free it is 54%); the data cleaning removes most negative reviews; and the justifications are a template. Be fair: the leak was in our first reproduction's example choice, not a claim about the authors. Next: two slides on how the method works, then three slides of evidence. |
| 5 | main talk | Phase 1 Data Preprocessing Pipeline | Original paper's pipeline (TextBlob DQC, stratified, VGST, neutral oversampling). Point forward: slide 9 shows TextBlob filtering hurts on Electronics. |
| 6 | main talk | Phase 1: LLaMA-3-8B + LoRA Fine-Tuning | LoRA explained. LoRA is still trained (Phase 1), but in the final stack it is an ablation row, not the main agent. |
| 7 | main talk | The One-Shot Label Leak Inflated Earlier Numbers | Leak audit. Picking a one-shot example whose star differs from the truth leaks about 8 points. All later numbers are zero-shot and leak-free. |
| 8 | main talk | What the Electronics Adapter Actually Generates | Hallucination study. LoRA explanations are a canned template; digit probabilities are the usable signal. That is why Phase 2 combines probabilities, not explanations. |
| 9 | main talk | TextBlob Filtering Hurts; VGST Adds Nothing | Preprocessing ablation. TextBlob DQC deletes most 1 and 2 star reviews; VGST picks long reviews; both are dropped. |
| 10 | main talk | Where Phase 2 Started: the Original Four-Agent Design | Original Phase 2 design (Analyst, Visual, RAG, Critic). Say: this was the starting design; the Oct 9 audit (Run 2) and later experiments replaced it with the probe + Evidence + Reflector system (slide 18). Slide 12 shows how the agent idea comes back in Phase 2 v3. |
| 11 | main talk | Phase 2 System: How a Review Is Rated and Explained | Phase 2 system. Walk the five boxes left to right. Decision core: Evidence model, LLaMA probe, Reflector (the main stack, built and frozen). Agentic layer: Router with escalation, optional LLM re-rating, Explainer and Critic loop, being built in LangGraph and each one measured. Self-correction happens at three points: escalation, re-rating, and the explanation loop. |
| 12 | main talk | Agents That Route, Explain and Check Themselves | How Phase 2 aims to solve the problem. Say: the specialists decide the star because an LLM choosing the star failed twice (Gate 0). The agents now do what LLMs are good at: routing, explaining, and checking explanations. Every explanation is checked by the Critic and measured on all 3,000 test reviews. A1 is running; DeBERTa runs on Colab Nov 1. Final demo is a local notebook. |
| 13 | main talk | Amazon Reviews 2023 Electronics: Frozen, Disjoint Splits | Protocol. Frozen disjoint splits; all choices on dev; each test split read once per declared config. Since Oct 24 there is also dev2 (2,000 balanced) for the Reflector. |
| 14 | main talk | Phase 1 Results: The Baseline Paper's Method | Phase 1 results. Say: this is the baseline paper's method retrained on Electronics, leak-free. Exact star 54.0 / 53.4, but within one star about 94% and positive vs negative 91-93%: it gets the direction right. On the paper's own Kaggle data with its protocol and no leak it reaches 69.1% (always-5 gives 63.8%). The paper's 92.6% used a different protocol; our old 70.7 / 60.1 were leaky and withdrawn. |
| 15 | main talk | Everything We Tried and Dropped (1 / 2) | Full ledger, part 1. Do not read every row. Pick three: the LLM judge (failed twice, which is why the LLM does not decide the star), the Visual Verifier (constant output), and the recalibration (the gain was the leak). Say: every rule was written before the run, on dev data only. |
| 16 | main talk | Everything We Tried and Dropped (2 / 2) | Full ledger, part 2. Message: more views of the same text, more LoRA data and fancier Reflectors did not help; what helped was more data for the probe and a bigger Reflector fit set. Note the honest near-miss: the 10K probe missed by .001 and only the 40K version passed. |
| 17 | main talk | What We Kept, and the Evidence for It | What we kept. Walk the ten rows quickly: each change has its evidence on the right. Together they give the main stack, 67.5% balanced eval and 75.7% natural test. |
| 18 | main talk | Main System: LLaMA Probe + Evidence Model Stack | MAIN RESULT. Probe + Evidence stack 67.5 eval / 75.7 natural, macro-F1 .675 / .612. Variance 65.8 +/- 0.6 and 75.4 +/- 0.8. Read the honest-read band aloud. |
| 19 | main talk | How Far Phase 2 Moves the Baseline | Phase 1 to Phase 2. Lead with the gain: +13.5 points on balanced eval and +22.3 on natural test, 29% and 48% fewer errors, significant after Holm. Then why: the agents complement (Evidence model on short reviews, probe on long ones). Say the caveat yourself: the earlier stack refit on the same dev reviews is only 2.0 / 1.5 behind. Never quote 70.7 / 60.1 (leaky), 74.8 (one seed) or 79.9 (class-mix correction). |
| 20 | main talk | All Models, Exact Accuracy with 95% Bootstrap CI | Bar chart of all frozen models with 95% CIs; main stack in red. Point out: base LLaMA zero-shot is weak (34%) but a probe on its hidden states reaches 61 / 74. |
| 21 | main talk | Does the Result Hold Up? Corrections, Errors, Calibration, Cost | Robustness. After Holm correction 5 of 8 comparisons stay significant, including the main stack vs the earlier LoRA + Evidence stack on both splits. Most errors are one star off. Calibration is good (ECE .05-.06). The probe costs 0.67 s per review, the rest is under 0.1 ms: that is why the next step adds a Router. |
| 22 | main talk | Phase 2 v3 Build Schedule | Build schedule, Oct 25 to Nov 5. Say: every row has its rule written first and is logged. Today the saved agents were rebuilt and match the frozen results exactly. The heavy runs (bigger probe, explanations on all 3,000 reviews, deletion test) run overnight on the charger. Freeze stage 1 on Nov 1, stage 2 on Nov 5. |
| 23 | main talk | Conclusions | Conclusions. Three cards: Phase 1 reproduced honestly (and two problems found in the original protocol); Phase 2's two-agent stack beats the single fine-tuned model, significantly; the agentic layer is being built and measured.
